subject: gk
question: Which of the following is the primary factor contributing to the dryness of old wells?

options.text: A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.
The ground surrounding the wells has been covered with a layer of vegetation,

solution:
The correct answer is __**A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary factor contributing to dryness of old wells:**

 
 
• A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas, leading to depletion of groundwater resources and drying up of old wells.
 
• Groundwater depletion is a major issue in many parts of the world due to increasing population and demand for water.
 
• Wells being covered may contribute to their abandonment, but not necessarily to their dryness.
 
• People stopping to utilize wells may be a consequence of their dryness, not the cause.
 
• Vegetation around wells may actually help retain moisture and prevent evaporation, but it is not the primary factor contributing to their dryness. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Boring pumps extract groundwater from aquifers, which are underground layers of permeable rock or soil that hold water.
 
• Overuse of groundwater resources can lead to depletion and even collapse of aquifers, causing wells to dry up.
 
• Groundwater depletion can also have other negative impacts, such as land subsidence, saltwater intrusion, and reduced streamflow.
 
• In some cases, old wells can be rehabilitated by deepening or re-drilling them, or by implementing sustainable groundwater management practices.
